Done. Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/text/ExtendedMessageFormatAgentTest.java` with 35 tests — all pass.

**Verification:**
```
defects4j compile  → OK (compile + compile.tests)
java -cp "$(defects4j export -p cp.test)" org.junit.runner.JUnitCore \
    org.apache.commons.lang3.text.ExtendedMessageFormatAgentTest
  → OK (35 tests)
```

**Style match:** followed the convention of the other `text`-package tests (`CompositeFormatTest`, `StrMatcherTest`, …) — JUnit 3 (`extends junit.framework.TestCase`, `testXxx()` methods, `(String name)` constructor, `assertEquals`/`assertTrue`/`fail()`-in-`catch`). The project bundles JUnit 4.7 but every test in this package uses the `junit.framework` API.

**Coverage (public API only):**
- **All four constructors** — default locale, explicit `Locale` (asserted via locale-sensitive number formatting: `1,234.50` US vs `1.234,50` de_DE), `Map` registry, and `Locale`+`Map`; plus null-registry equivalence to the no-registry path.
- **`toPattern()`** — round-trips plain patterns, custom-format elements (`{0,upper}`), format styles (`{0,echo,STYLE}`), repeated args, and re-inserts custom names after a `super` round-trip.
- **Custom `FormatFactory` behavior** — custom format applied to output, overriding a built-in name (`number`), name/arguments string passed to the factory (`STYLE` vs `null`), unknown names delegating to `MessageFormat`'s built-ins (`choice`), quoted/escaped-quote handling.
- **`applyPattern()`** — replacing a prior pattern, and adding a custom format on re-apply (observable via `format()` output and `toPattern()`).
- **Error/boundary cases** — `IllegalArgumentException` for unterminated element `{0`, unterminated description `{0,upper`, non-numeric index `{abc}`, malformed pattern without registry; `NullPointerException` for null pattern (with and without registry); empty and literal-only patterns.
- **Disabled mutators** — `setFormat`, `setFormatByArgumentIndex`, `setFormats`, `setFormatsByArgumentIndex` each assert `UnsupportedOperationException`.
- **`equals`/`hashCode`** — reflexive + consistent hashCode; equal instances and equal-but-distinct registry maps produce equal objects with equal hashCodes; inequality for differing registries, one null registry, differing patterns, `null`, a `String`, a plain `MessageFormat` with the same pattern (no `ClassCastException`), and a concrete subclass instance (`getClass()` guard).
